literal: Thinking of [it] the intoxication, and seeing [it] the delight, to liquor is not there, to love is there.
translation: To feel intoxicated just by thinking of it, and to feel delighted just by seeing it—these belong not to liquor, but only to love.
modern: நினைத்த உடனே களிப்பு அடைதலும், நேரில் கண்ட உடனே மகிழ்ச்சி அடைதலும் ஆகிய இவ்விரண்டும் மதுவுக்கு இல்லை; ஆனால் காமத்திற்கு உண்டு.
explanation: This couplet compares the effects of liquor and love. While liquor can only intoxicate after it is consumed, love has the unique power to intoxicate the mind the very moment one thinks of the beloved. Similarly, merely seeing the beloved brings immediate delight. The poet contrasts these two experiences to show that the joy of love is far superior and more immediate than any physical stimulant.
